definitions.gloss: conclusion; final touch; wrapping up; summing up
definitions.explanation: The final part or finishing touch of something — a speech, event, project, or year. Emphasizes bringing things to a proper close.

examples.japanese: {一年|いちねん}の{締|し}めくくりとして{忘年会|ぼうねんかい}を{開|ひら}く。
examples.english: We hold a year-end party as a way to wrap up the year.

examples.japanese: スピーチの{締|し}めくくりに{感謝|かんしゃ}の{言葉|ことば}を{述|の}べた。
examples.english: I expressed words of gratitude to conclude my speech.

examples.japanese: {今|こん}シーズンの{締|し}めくくりにふさわしい{試合|しあい}だった。
examples.english: It was a fitting game to wrap up this season.

notes:
From the verb {締|し}めくくる (to conclude, to wrap up). The noun form refers to the conclusion or final part of something, with an emphasis on bringing it to a satisfying or proper end.

USAGE:
Often used with の or として to express 'as the conclusion of.' Very common at the end of the year ({一年|いちねん}の{締|し}めくくり), at the end of events, or when finishing projects.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一年|いちねん}の{締|し}めくくり: wrapping up the year
- シーズンの{締|し}めくくり: conclusion of the season
- {締|し}めくくりの{挨拶|あいさつ}: closing remarks
- {締|し}めくくりとして: as a conclusion

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {結|むす}び: conclusion, closing — more literary, often used for the end of essays or books
- {仕上|しあ}げ: finishing touch — emphasizes the final polish or completion of work
- {最後|さいご}: the end, the last — neutral, simply refers to the final point without the nuance of 'wrapping up'
